current_suggestion.pitch: Mauboussin sits at the intersection of mental models, decision-making under uncertainty, and probabilistic thinking — covering the same Munger/Kahneman territory you care about but from a rigorous investment-research background that grounds the ideas in real data and base rates. His work on skill vs. luck, reference class forecasting, and the psychology of judgment goes deeper than what Lex or Huberman touch on in passing, without drifting into generic self-help. Primarily solo lectures and structured talks rather than long-form interviews, which makes the frameworks easier to extract and apply.
